candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — equipment safety and prevention of medication-administration errors
candidate.educational_objective: Explain how anti-free-flow mechanisms reduce uncontrolled IV infusion and overdose risk.

options.A: Prevent uncontrolled gravity flow of IV fluid or medication when the set is not being controlled by the pump.
options.B: Increase the programmed infusion rate when an occlusion occurs.
options.C: Eliminate the need to monitor the infusion and patient.
options.D: Convert an IV administration set into an enteral feeding set.

candidate.rationale: FDA device safety information identifies uncontrolled flow and over-infusion as serious infusion-pump hazards. FDA recall information involving anti-free-flow components demonstrates that failure to clamp tubing after removal from a pump can permit free flow and cause dangerous medication over-infusion. Therefore A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Infusion-pump failures can cause over-infusion; anti-free-flow components are designed to prevent uncontrolled fluid flow when administration tubing is removed from pump control.
candidate.source_document_title: Infusion Pumps; Class I Device Recall — Infusomat Space Pump
candidate.source_locator: Infusion Pumps — safety issues causing over-infusion; Recall ID 109869 — anti-free-flow clip/catch and tubing free-flow protection
candidate.source_version_date: Current FDA infusion-pump safety page; recall evidence retained as device-mechanism example
candidate.stem: What is the safety purpose of an anti-free-flow mechanism in an IV infusion administration set?
